paths.description: Public mobile race-information homepage and navigation hub; represents the highest-traffic entry template.
Leading-information listing; represents compact data/list templates.
Featured-race detail hub; represents the public race-detail journey.
JRA app landing page; represents promotional content and download conversion.
Linked IPAT login entry; represents the public edge of the wagering/account journey. No authenticated wagering was attempted.
Synthetic missing route used to inspect HTTP failure and recovery behaviour.

findings.summary: The site does not adapt to the user’s dark colour-scheme preference.
findings.evidence: The dark-emulated screenshot is visually identical to the light mobile page, and the platform probe found no color-scheme declaration or prefers-color-scheme rule.
findings.suggestedFix: Declare color-scheme and provide preference-driven dark surface, text, border, and media treatments with light-dark() or a prefers-color-scheme fallback.

findings.summary: The autoplay hero continues changing when reduced motion is requested.
findings.evidence: Under prefers-reduced-motion: reduce, the active hero changed from 2026_jra-summercp-2026-3.webp to 2026_sumahokeiba.webp after six seconds.
findings.suggestedFix: Disable autoplay and non-essential transitions under prefers-reduced-motion: reduce, while retaining explicit previous/next controls.

findings.summary: State and route changes use abrupt legacy swaps rather than View Transitions.
findings.evidence: The computed CSS corpus contains no view-transition usage; public race links navigate through legacy POST/JS actions.
findings.suggestedFix: Use same-document or cross-document View Transitions for menu, tab, and route changes, with a reduced-motion fallback.

findings.summary: The long page has no scroll-state-aware navigation or progress affordance.
findings.evidence: The homepage is 6,014 CSS pixels tall, while CSS inspection found no scroll-state container-query or scroll-timeline implementation.
findings.suggestedFix: Let the header compact after scrolling and expose useful section/position feedback without covering content.

findings.summary: Two fixed promotional banners reduce the usable mobile viewport on first load.
findings.evidence: The 360x800 screenshot shows “はじめての方へ” and “JRAアプリ” bars stacked across the bottom, each covering content until separately dismissed.
findings.suggestedFix: Avoid showing both promotions together; defer them until relevant and provide one clear, accessible light-dismiss action.

findings.summary: Interactive overlays and controls are built from custom divs and hash links rather than native primitives.
findings.evidence: DOM/CSS probing found 0 dialog, 0 popover and 0 details elements, 26 custom role=button elements, and 31 href="#" anchors; Lighthouse also found malformed ARIA relationships.
findings.suggestedFix: Use button elements for actions, dialog for modal search, popover for transient UI, and details/summary for disclosures; rely on native focus and dismissal.

findings.summary: Responsive behaviour is viewport-only rather than component-aware.
findings.evidence: Both tested templates fit 360px without overflow, but the CSS corpus contains no @container rules despite reused cards, tabs and navigation modules.
findings.suggestedFix: Add containment and size/container queries where reusable modules change layout based on available space.

findings.summary: Failure states expose terse server errors without recovery actions.
findings.evidence: A missing route renders Japanese text saying access is forbidden plus “(403:FORBIDDEN)”, with no retry, search, homepage CTA, or contextual explanation in the main error area.
findings.suggestedFix: Serve a real 404/403 template with a clear explanation, homepage/search actions, preserved navigation, and an announced status message.

findings.summary: The mobile load misses the LCP performance bar by a wide margin.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse measured FCP 5.6s, LCP 14.1s, Speed Index 12.6s and TTI 20.6s (performance 0.51); the independent trace measured FCP 4.16s and LCP 5.74s. CLS remained good.
findings.suggestedFix: Prioritise the hero/LCP asset, shorten critical dependencies, defer non-critical imagery and scripts, and verify under mobile throttling.

findings.summary: The page ships a large, eager critical path with blocking styles/scripts and images lacking loading controls.
findings.evidence: HAR recorded 156 requests and 4.74MB transferred, including 110 images/3.60MB; 9 parser-inserted stylesheets and a synchronous head script were render-blocking candidates. All 100 inspected images lacked width/height and 52 below-fold images lacked lazy loading.
findings.suggestedFix: Reserve image dimensions, lazy-load below-fold media, preload only the LCP image, consolidate critical CSS, and defer/module non-critical scripts.

findings.summary: Unused third-party and legacy code materially inflates the load.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse estimated 301KiB unused JavaScript and 37KiB unused CSS; multiple GTM/gtag bundles and Facebook scripts dominate the waste.
findings.suggestedFix: Remove duplicate analytics loaders, gate optional tags on consent/need, split page code, and subset icon/CSS bundles.

findings.summary: ARIA roles and accessible names are malformed in core navigation.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse accessibility was 0.84 and found prohibited aria-label on roleless divs, tabs without the required tablist parent, a tablist with invalid children, visible-label/name mismatches, and orphaned list items.
findings.suggestedFix: Rebuild the quick menu and tabs with semantic lists/buttons and a conforming tablist/tab/tabpanel hierarchy; keep visible and accessible names aligned.

findings.summary: Pages lack a main landmark and have weak document heading semantics.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse found no main landmark; DOM inspection shows the H1 contains only the logo image and key content starts at H2. Focus itself was visibly outlined.
findings.suggestedFix: Wrap primary content in main, give each template a descriptive text H1, and retain the existing skip link and visible focus treatment.

findings.summary: A third-party impression endpoint causes a console security error.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse recorded refusal to execute pp.d2-apps.net’s image/gif response as JavaScript.
findings.suggestedFix: Fix or remove the JSONP-style impression endpoint and ensure script responses use a JavaScript MIME type.

findings.summary: Image markup is not dimensionally sound.
findings.evidence: The images primitive found 100/100 images without width/height; Lighthouse found carousel pager images displayed at 8x5 despite 10x10 source aspect ratio.
findings.suggestedFix: Add intrinsic width/height or aspect-ratio and correct the pager asset sizing so layout and pixels match.

findings.summary: Many core race actions are not crawlable links.
findings.evidence: The rendered DOM contains 31 href="#" anchors; race card, odds and results use onclick POST actions. Lighthouse also flagged generic link text.
findings.suggestedFix: Expose stable href URLs for public race data and enhance them with JavaScript rather than replacing navigation with onclick/POST.

findings.summary: Robots and sitemap endpoints do not provide valid crawler files.
findings.evidence: Direct requests to /robots.txt and /sitemap.xml returned 403 and the homepage HTML; the mobile homepage canonical also points to https://www.jra.go.jp/ rather than its fetched URL.
findings.suggestedFix: Serve valid 200 text/plain robots.txt and XML sitemap responses, and verify canonical/alternate signals intentionally consolidate equivalent desktop/mobile URLs.

findings.summary: The organization homepage has social tags but no structured data.
findings.evidence: The document probe found complete basic Open Graph fields but zero JSON-LD blocks.
findings.suggestedFix: Add accurate Organization/WebSite JSON-LD and validate it against visible content and canonical URLs.

findings.summary: Cookie and CSP defaults are not secure enough.
findings.evidence: HTTPS/HSTS/nosniff/frame protection are present, but CSP is absent. All 7 observed first-party cookies lacked Secure; 5 used SameSite=None and two analytics cookies persist for 400 days.
findings.suggestedFix: Set Secure and an explicit appropriate SameSite value on every cookie, shorten analytics retention, and deploy a nonce/hash-based CSP.

findings.summary: Tracking is extensive and begins without an evident consent or minimisation layer.
findings.evidence: The page contacted 13 third-party origins and five known tracker domains; 26 third-party requests transferred 776KB, including Google, DoubleClick, Facebook, Yahoo and D2 tags.
findings.suggestedFix: Inventory and remove non-essential tags, load analytics only after an appropriate choice/context, batch necessary telemetry, and document retention/purpose.

findings.summary: The linked wagering login relies on subscriber number, PIN and P-ARS credentials with no visible phishing-resistant option.
findings.evidence: The IPAT login screenshot shows three knowledge-factor fields and no passkey/WebAuthn route. No permission prompt fired on the public homepage.
findings.suggestedFix: Offer passkeys/WebAuthn as the preferred sign-in or reauthentication method while retaining a proportionate recovery path.

findings.summary: Several browser-enforced privacy policies are missing.
findings.evidence: Headers inspection found no Referrer-Policy or Permissions-Policy; CSP/frame-ancestors is also absent on the main document, although X-Frame-Options SAMEORIGIN is present.
findings.suggestedFix: Add a strict Referrer-Policy, least-privilege Permissions-Policy, and CSP frame-ancestors directive; evaluate Trusted Types for script-sensitive surfaces.

findings.summary: Public race actions depend on JavaScript and POST navigation.
findings.evidence: Although 94% of rendered content words occur in raw HTML, primary race-card/odds/result anchors have href="#" and onclick doAction handlers, so those journeys disappear without scripting.
findings.suggestedFix: Give each public action a real GET URL and layer enhanced POST/state behaviour on top.

findings.summary: The network/HTTP error template is a dead end.
findings.evidence: The synthetic missing path displays a raw 403 label without contextual recovery controls, despite global footer links.
findings.suggestedFix: Return the correct status and an actionable error view with retry, search and safe navigation options.

findings.summary: The wagering login does not expose autofill semantics on visible credential fields.
findings.evidence: IPAT DOM inspection found visible userid, password and P-ARS inputs with no name or autocomplete tokens; the screenshot confirms these are the core sign-in fields.
findings.suggestedFix: Add stable names and correct autocomplete tokens (username/current-password where semantically appropriate), with labels bound by for/id.

findings.summary: Image delivery is disproportionate for a mobile portal.
findings.evidence: The homepage transferred 3.60MB across 110 images; 43 images use legacy formats, 39 lack responsive sources, 13 are oversized, and a promotional PNG alone is 442KB.
findings.suggestedFix: Use AVIF/WebP where suitable, responsive srcset/sizes, properly sized raster assets and lazy loading for below-fold/decorative media.

findings.summary: Background carousel and analytics work runs without user demand.
findings.evidence: The hero kept auto-advancing under reduced motion and 13 third-party origins initiated tracking/network work on page load.
findings.suggestedFix: Stop non-essential autoplay, defer background work until visible/idle, and condition telemetry on purpose and user choice.

findings.summary: Third-party and media budgets are too high for the page’s informational purpose.
findings.evidence: HAR measured 4.74MB total, 776KB third party, 3.60MB images and 884KB scripts on one homepage load.
findings.suggestedFix: Set template-specific byte/request budgets, remove duplicate tags, and defer promotional/media modules until near the viewport.

taskList.title: Fix LCP and mobile critical-path delivery
Replace hash-link/custom ARIA navigation with semantic controls and real URLs
Minimise tracking and harden cookies/security headers
Optimise the image and media budget
Reduce stacked promotions and use native dismissal primitives
Modernise IPAT authentication and autofill semantics
Repair robots, sitemap, canonical and structured metadata
Fix third-party console and asset-markup errors
Add View Transitions with reduced-motion fallback
